transcript.text: In this video, we'll walk you through how to make your on print shop store SEO friendly to help your website rank higher on search engines and attract more visitors.

We'll cover everything from connecting your domain to Google Search Console and configuring SEO settings for products, categories, and pages to setting up site maps, URL redirections, and product feeds.
Before getting started, ensure your domain is live and connected to Google Search Console.
This allows you to monitor how Google indexes your website.
Also, make sure user friendly URLs and schema markup are enabled under your site settings.
These settings help search engines better understand your content and improve how your pages appear in search results.
Let's start by optimizing SEO for your products.
To configure this, go to Products, select Print Products or Ready to Buy Products.
Open the action menu and select the meta tag section for the desired product.
Here you can define the meta tag for the default section, Browse Design, Upload Design, or Custom Design.
Let's select Default here.
Now enter the page title that is displayed on the browser tab and Search result listings.
Meta description that briefly describes the page content and heavily influences your product ranking.
Canonical reference that prevents duplicate content issues if similar product URLs exist.
Additional schema markup makes your listings richer in search results and additional meta tags for more SEO flexibility.
Once you've filled in the details, click save.
As a best practice, use natural and descriptive keywords such as the product type, material, or finish.
For example, instead of just business cards, use custom business cards.
300 GSM matte finish.
Avoid repeating the same keyword too often as this can reduce your SEO effectiveness.
Next, optimize your product categories.
For this, go to Products, select Product categories, click Edit on the category you want to optimize and scroll to the SEO content description section.
Enter the page title, meta description, canonical reference, and schema markup.
Then click Save.
For instance, you can set a page title like Marketing Materials, Printing Online, and a meta description such as Explore Custom Printing for brochures, Flyers, and business stationery.
Your content pages like About Us services or FAQ also play an important role in improving SEO and building trust with visitors.
To optimize these, navigate to the Content Management, then select Contents from the Dynamic Pages or Fixed Content tab.
Select the page you want to update, move to the SEO Settings section, and enter the appropriate page title, meta description, canonical reference, additional schema, markup, and meta tag.
If there are pages that you don't want to appear in search results, such as Privacy Policy or Terms and Conditions, enable the Exclude in Site Map option.
Click Save when done.
After that, to manage your global SEO settings, move to the SEO section and click on the Page title keyword setting.
This section lets you manage meta titles, descriptions, and schema markup for different areas of your store, such as products, product categories, template categories, content pages, and other pages.
Once all SEO fields are configured, it's time to generate your sitemap from the SEO section.
Let's now move to the Sitemap section.
Under the Generate tab, click Generate to create the default XML file.
You can then edit the sitemap from the Edit tab or upload your own version.
In the Settings section, you can define the priority of pages, select how often they should be crawled, and specify the last modified date.
These settings ensure that your latest updates are captured when search engines crawl your website.
Let's generate your Shopping feeds which allow your product information to appear on platforms like Google Shopping and Facebook Shops.
In this video, we will be covering the steps for generating Google Feeds.
Please note that similar steps apply to the Facebook Feeds generation.
To create them, move to the Google Feeds tab.
Start by configuring the fields.
Some of the fields are by default configured.
You can modify or delete some of the system configured fields as per requirement.
If you want to add more fields to the feeds, you can select from the Additional Fields drop down menu.
Let's add MPN field to the settings.
Select MPN from the drop down menu and then select the value for the same.
Here you will have three options to choose from.
You can either add a default value, refer to the CSV for the added value or set product SKU as the MPN.
Once configured, click on Add and this will appear in the list above with the option to change the value or delete this configuration.
Similarly, you can add other fields or custom fields.
Regarding custom fields, you can add up to 5 for seasonal, sale, clearance, etc.
Moving to the Product Settings section, you can generate feeds for all products, include specific products or exclude specific products.
Later.
If you have added an CSV reference value in the field Settings, then download the file, fill up the appropriate data and then upload the file.
After all the configuration, click Generate to create your XML feed file.
Additionally, you can add optional product feed variants under Product Feed Variant.
These variants let you include different product option combinations such as size, material, or finish within your feed.
To create a feed variant, move to the Product Feed Variant tab and click the Add button.
From the drop down, select the product you want to include in the feed.
Next, choose the size, quantity, and any additional product options to create specific combinations.
Once you've made your selections, check the preview to review the variance, links and title.
Select the check box against the links to include in the feed, and then click on the Save.
Once the Shopping feeds are generated, it is time to upload the feed file to Google Merchant Center for Google Shopping or to Facebook Catalog Manager for Facebook Shops.
Next, you can also manage meta tag settings to view or add tags for different pages.
From here, select a page, select the type, enter the meta name and content description, and save your changes.
Next, configure your robots dot TXT file, which tells search engines which pages they are allowed or not allowed to crawl.
Your system includes A preconfigured robots dot TXT file with recommended settings, but you can modify it as needed.
Now let's talk about URL redirection.
When you change or remove a page URL, setting up a redirect ensures that visitors and search engines are automatically guided to the correct page instead of landing on an error.
This helps preserve your SEO rankings.
To manage redirects, go to Manage URL Redirection section under SEO.
To further enhance your SEO performance, don't forget to optimize your image.
All text.
Search engines can't read images, so all text helps them understand what an image represents.
From the On Print Shop solution, you can add alt text to images added to the product and category section.
For example, let's select the product section and the store to view the image details and set the alt text for an accordion fold brochure as custom accordion fold brochures with glossy finish.
This improves accessibility and helps your images appear in Google Image search results, driving additional traffic to your store.
And that's it, you've now completed all the essential steps to make your on print shop store SEO friendly.
Thanks for tuning in.
